invariant: Every tranche identifier referenced by a canonical or architecture document must resolve to exactly one tranche definition in the live sequencing authority (docs/ROADMAP.md), and renaming or retiring a tranche identifier must not leave dependent documents gating work on an identifier the roadmap no longer defines.
observation: In the same merge that renamed the L0 tranche to L0-SEM-NORM-A and folded L2-FORMA-KB0 into "L2-FORMA-0 + bounded KB0", two identifiers ceased to exist anywhere in docs/ROADMAP.md (git grep -c over docs/ROADMAP.md at 8a5be7fd returns 0 for both "L2-FORMA-KB0" and "L2-FORMA-5"), yet dependent documents still gate on them: docs/architecture/MONETA_SYSTEM1_SYSTEM2_ONNX_ARCHITECTURE.md:206 ("versioned Forma case/template/contraindication features once L2-FORMA-KB0 is qualified") and docs/architecture/FULL_MONETA_SEMANTIC_EMBODIMENT_ARCHITECTURE_PLAN.md:1013 ("### L2-FORMA-5 - feedback/study expansion, still non-adaptive"). The same merge also leaves docs/ROADMAP.md internally inconsistent: line 35 (FM3 capability-ladder row) still says L0-SEM-NORM while the tranche table in the same file defines L0-SEM-NORM-A, and bare L0-SEM-NORM appears 3 times in FULL_MONETA_SEMANTIC_EMBODIMENT_ARCHITECTURE_PLAN.md and once in docs/roadmap/P1_FULL_MONETA_INCREMENTAL_CAPABILITY_PLAN.md. L5-FORMA-SYNTH-1 was checked and still resolves (docs/ROADMAP.md:67), so it is not part of this observation.
hypothesis: The tranche table was rewritten without a cross-reference pass over documents that gate sequencing on tranche identifiers, so an implementer reading MONETA_SYSTEM1_SYSTEM2_ONNX_ARCHITECTURE.md would conclude Forma knowledge-base qualification is a separate later tranche instead of part of L2-FORMA-0, and would plan L2-FORMA-5 work against a tranche the roadmap retired.
reproducer: git grep -c "L2-FORMA-KB0" 8a5be7fd -- docs/ROADMAP.md; git grep -c "L2-FORMA-5" 8a5be7fd -- docs/ROADMAP.md; git grep -n "L2-FORMA-KB0" 8a5be7fd -- docs/architecture/MONETA_SYSTEM1_SYSTEM2_ONNX_ARCHITECTURE.md; git grep -n "L2-FORMA-5" 8a5be7fd -- docs/architecture/FULL_MONETA_SEMANTIC_EMBODIMENT_ARCHITECTURE_PLAN.md; git show 8a5be7fd:docs/ROADMAP.md | sed -n "35p"

invariant: Any research-context field that can alter an investigation perspective or Moneta intent must either participate in committed persistence/digest identity or be explicitly excluded by a governed contract before L1 perspective implementation can claim replayable identity.
observation: At main@44f3f0b4, src/atlas/types.ts declares six ResearchContext fields: studyId, researchQuestion, hypothesis, variablesOfInterest, currentTask, observerMode. The domain ResearchContextOptions/class carries only the first three, and InvestigationAggregate.toState() persists only those three. PR #930 independently reports the same three-field projection in all committed-context paths and notes that production Moneta does not yet consume intent. Therefore variablesOfInterest/currentTask/observerMode can be represented in the declared Atlas context type but are not currently committed by the aggregate persistence identity that L1-PERSPECTIVE-0 is preparing to build on.
hypothesis: If L1 perspective semantics consume any of the three uncommitted fields without first extending or explicitly excluding them from identity, two semantically different perspectives could share the same persisted/digest identity and replay could silently reconstruct the wrong investigative context.
reproducer: At main@44f3f0b4 compare src/atlas/types.ts ResearchContext with src/atlas/domain/ResearchContext.ts ResearchContextOptions/getters and InvestigationAggregate.toState()/computeDigest researchContext projections; then construct two otherwise identical candidate L1 contexts differing only in variablesOfInterest and verify whether current persisted state/digest can distinguish them. Do not treat a helper-only type test as closure; exercise the production commit/digest path.

invariant: RFC 0011 context bindings used to prevent cross-investigation, cross-dataset, cross-scope, or cross-runtime adoption must fail closed when a required identity dimension is absent as well as when it differs; an omitted binding must not behave as a wildcard.
observation: PR #957 adds investigationId, datasetFingerprint, scopeId and runtimeGeneration as optional fields, then checkContextCompatibility compares each dimension only when both captured and active values are defined. Consequently an active context lacking datasetFingerprint/investigationId/scopeId/runtimeGeneration can be accepted against a captured binding carrying that dimension, and vice versa, provided contextId/nodeId/epoch match. The adversarial test exercises unequal populated dataset fingerprints but does not exercise missing-versus-present identity fields. PR #957 nevertheless claims RFC 0011 context bindings now fail closed against dataset fingerprint mismatches and that FMA-06 is fully resolved. Exact-head CI and CodeQL are green.
hypothesis: The repair treated optional legacy compatibility as equivalent to fail-closed identity enforcement, leaving absence of newly introduced identity dimensions as an implicit wildcard.
reproducer: At main@aa746c2b create/commit a context without datasetFingerprint, obtain its activation, construct a captured ContextBinding using that activation's contextId/nodeId/activationEpoch but add datasetFingerprint:'different-dataset', then call checkContextCompatibility(captured, activation). Observe ok:true because the dataset comparison executes only when both values are defined. Repeat for investigationId, scopeId or runtimeGeneration.

artifact: PR #958 head 02cb70c1e38405be487b0723f59af5f5d0996e66; merged main via 96e3ef8b70f01be206beabdd9714aa1372659def; src/learning/FormaPriorEvaluator.ts; tests/fma-11-13-learning-authority.test.ts
invariant: FMA-12 safety/admissibility rates used to authorize model promotion must be finite, valid measurements in their declared domain and satisfy the mandatory threshold; merely being a JavaScript number must not constitute admissible evidence.
observation: FormaPriorEvaluator.evaluate() rejects knownAnswerPassRate and abstentionComplianceRate only when undefined or typeof !== 'number', then rejects values only when < 1.0. JavaScript NaN has typeof 'number' and NaN < 1.0 is false; positive Infinity and values >1 likewise evade the threshold check. Therefore NaN can satisfy both mandatory safety-rate gates without representing any measurement. The FMA-12 falsifier tests omitted rates but does not exercise NaN, Infinity, negative values, or values above the metric domain. PR #958 states these rates are 'explicitly measured' and mandatory at 1.0. Exact-head CI, CodeQL and approval-gate are green.
hypothesis: The repair correctly removed the previous implicit 1.0 default but equated numeric type presence with metric admissibility, leaving non-finite/out-of-domain values outside the fail-closed contract.
reproducer: Construct a corpus/candidate for which candidateAccuracy exceeds baselineAccuracy and holdoutCount meets the minimum. Call evaluate(candidate, corpus, {modelId:'x',modelVersion:'1',knownAnswerPassRate:NaN,abstentionComplianceRate:NaN}). Observe that neither safety-rate check adds a refusal reason and passedGate can become true. Repeat with Infinity or >1 values. A valid rate-domain guard should instead require Number.isFinite(rate) && rate >= 0 && rate <= 1 before applying the 1.0 threshold.

invariant: FM8 multi-family composition must bind each selected representation primitive to semantically compatible governed evidence; absent a compatible snapshot it must refuse rather than silently substitute unrelated evidence.
observation: PR #962 attempts to repair FMA-10/SHADOW-0016 by selecting a snapshot using family === prim.kind, then falling back to snapshotsList[i], then the primary snapshot. Representation primitive kinds and analytical snapshot families are not demonstrated to share a canonical identity vocabulary, and the fallback permits a primitive to receive evidence solely because it occupies the same array position. If there are fewer snapshots than primitives, remaining primitives receive the primary snapshot. The new FMA-10 test verifies graph relationships/absence of phantom edges but does not assert that each primitive received a semantically compatible slice. PR #962 nevertheless declares FMA-10 resolved. Exact-head CI and CodeQL are green.
hypothesis: The repair replaced unconditional slice reuse with heuristic positional evidence assignment without introducing a governed primitive-to-semantic-source binding, so topology fidelity improved while semantic embodiment authority remains under-specified.
reproducer: Construct a selected graph with three semantically distinct primitives and provide snapshots:[snapshotAgg,snapshotDist]. Ensure the third primitive's kind is incompatible with the aggregate snapshot. Run synthesizeOrAdapt and inspect composedState: the third primitive is registered using the primary aggregate-derived slice rather than refusing. Separately reverse the snapshots array where family/kind matching does not resolve and observe positional assignment can change which evidence embodies a primitive without changing the selected graph.

invariant: A claim that persisted System-1 advice is used for replay must be demonstrated by restoring the persisted artifact and exercising the replay/adaptation path without rerunning or substituting the proposer; serialization presence alone establishes preservation, not replay consumption.
observation: PR #966 correctly adds system1ProposalSet to FullMonetaSynthesisResult and FormaInvestigationStateV1 and serializes it through exportFormaInvestigationBytes(). NemosyneSession restoration decodes formaInvestigationSnapshot and calls setFormaState(parsed), so the proposal set survives restoration. However InvestigationAggregate.adaptRepresentation() still calls FullMonetaEngine.synthesizeOrAdapt(), which unconditionally constructs FormaSystem1Proposer and calls generateProposals() before search. No restored system1ProposalSet is supplied to that path. The new round-trip test only JSON.parse()s exported bytes and compares the embedded value; it never restores a NemosyneSession and performs replay/adaptation while proving the proposer was not rerun. PR #966 states that 'replay uses the recorded advisory result instead of rerunning inference' and lists frozen-prior replay only as deferred. Exact-head CI, CodeQL and approval-gate are green.
hypothesis: The tranche implemented durable capture/restoration of consumed advice but promoted preservation into replay-consumption semantics before a replay path capable of injecting the recorded proposal set existed.
reproducer: At main@13ecc641 create an investigation whose adaptation produces a known system1ProposalSet; serialize/restore through NemosyneSession; confirm getFormaState() retains that set. Then invoke adaptRepresentation() on the restored investigation while instrumenting or substituting FormaSystem1Proposer.generateProposals(), or change inputs that alter proposer output. Observe adaptation calls generateProposals() again rather than consuming the restored set. Independently note that tests/fm5-s1-consumed-record.test.ts performs byte JSON round-trip only and contains no restored-session replay assertion.

InvestigationAggregate stores the direct compile result only in _activeDirectCompileResult. PR #991 nevertheless states critiques are 'durably recorded' with investigator attribution; PR #994's own post-review explicitly defers 'critique-ledger echo without validation'.

Observe the object is copied into result.critiqueLedger without refusal. Then serialize/restore the investigation through the normal durable session/state path and check whether the critique survives; current DSE1 evidence only proves same-call/result echo.
